body.text: Epworth HealthCare review triggered by Four Corners allegations backs private provider's governance
In short:
Epworth HealthCare has accepted 21 recommendations made in an independent review of the private healthcare provider’s clinical governance.
The review was launched after Four Corners revealed allegations that a surgeon performed unnecessary operations on women for endometriosis.
It found the provider's clinical governance framework was "robust" and "detailed".
An independent review of the Melbourne hospital where a gynaecologist who allegedly performed unnecessary operations on women worked has found "no significant gaps" in its governance framework.
But the review made 21 recommendations, including more oversight of procedures that could affect women's fertility, which Epworth HealthCare has adopted.
Earlier this year, Four Corners revealed allegations that Simon Gordon repeatedly removed tissue and organs from women for "severe" endometriosis, when pathology showed little trace of the disease.
Some patients underwent life-altering procedures to remove ovaries, fallopian tubes and their uteruses.
After the episode aired, Epworth HealthCare — Victoria's largest private healthcare provider — commissioned an independent panel to review its clinical governance arrangements.

The review released on Wednesday found the policies and guidelines that make up the operator's clinical governance were "robust" and "detailed", but chief executive Andrew Stripp conceded the findings did not lessen the impact of the patient's experiences.
"I recognise that the recent reporting has been distressing for many patients and their families, and I am sorry for the worry and uncertainty this has caused," Professor Stripp said in a statement.
The review did not examine Dr Gordon's practice itself.
Among the 21 recommendations was a proposal for peer-to-peer insight or multidisciplinary input when medical treatment with the potential to compromise fertility is being considered.
In response, Epworth HealthCare has vowed to introduce a requirement for a multidisciplinary review for such gynaecological procedures.

The review also found Epworth staff and executives did not thoroughly understand how external regulatory bodies such as the Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency (AHPRA) and medical boards "could or should" be involved in Epworth's clinical governance frameworks.
The hospital was also urged to improve its processes for receiving and reviewing patient feedback.

"Feedback mechanisms should be established to ensure those who raise concerns or report incidents are aware that appropriate consideration has been given to those reports [within privacy and confidentiality boundaries]," the review said.
Another area highlighted was the way the hospital generated, collected and analysed data on surgical procedures.
The review found that the provider’s current system, like that of many other hospitals, relied on manual data handling and analysis "which inherently results in inefficiencies and inaccuracies".

However, the review found the hospital was already in the process of improving its data and analytics to provide clinicians and leaders with better information about patterns of practice, patient outcomes and risks.

Dr Gordon has previously maintained he acted ethically and responsibly, telling the ABC he "never performed surgery to treat endometriosis or any other condition unless I was absolutely convinced it was in the patient's best interest and to improve their overall quality of life".
He retired from practice shortly after Epworth discovered in October 2025 that Four Corners was investigating him and removed himself from AHPRA’s register of practitioners in December.
The regulator began reviewing previous complaints it received and launched a fresh investigation into Dr Gordon earlier this year.

Last month, the ABC revealed that the Medical Board of Australia, which registers practitioners, had referred the former gynaecologist to a Victorian tribunal alleging he engaged in professional misconduct.
Victoria Police ended an investigation into the gynaecologist, saying it was unable to take the matter further, earlier this month.
